entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Eadberht II was the king of Kent from 616 CE, jointly with Sigered. He is believed to have been the son of Æðelberht II. Eadberht II's reign was marked by his efforts to Christianize the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Kent, which had previously been a pagan stronghold. The king's Christianization efforts were influenced by his marriage to Bertha, the daughter of King Sigebert of Austrasia, a Frankish king who had converted to Christianity.

The Christianization of Kent had significant consequences, including the conversion of the Kentish population and the establishment of a Christian church in the kingdom. Eadberht II's Christianization efforts also had an impact on the broader Anglo-Saxon world, as other kingdoms began to adopt Christianity.

Eadberht II's legacy as a Christianizing king has been subject to debate among historians, with some viewing him as a key figure in the spread of Christianity in Anglo-Saxon England. His reign also saw significant cultural and economic changes, including the establishment of trade relationships with the Frankish kingdom.

The exact date of Eadberht II's birth is unknown, but it is believed to have been sometime before 616 CE. He died in 764 CE.
